subject.title: fix(codex): clean final/yield turn close writes a false "user interrupted" marker into the thread rollout

question: Should an explicit Codex terminal delivery wait for natural `turn/completed` for up to 10 seconds, with immediate interruption only for a new inbound message or the deadline, rather than preserve immediate `turn/interrupt` closure?
rationale: The patch is a deliberate user-visible lifecycle-policy change: it removes false clean-close abort markers but trades immediate terminal settlement for a bounded grace period and retains an exceptional fallback marker.

options.title: Adopt bounded natural completion
options.body: Keep the proposed 10-second absolute grace period, then require a clean rebase and refreshed exact-head live proof.

options.title: Keep immediate interruption
options.body: Preserve current immediate close behavior and accept the false marker until an upstream graceful-stop protocol exists.

options.title: Choose a different terminal policy
options.body: Request a different grace duration or post-final/inbound policy before implementation is refreshed.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded natural completion
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed 10-second absolute grace period, then require a clean rebase and refreshed exact-head live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the authoritative Codex turn-finalization boundary that this proposal extends.
